For a spin–½ particle (such as a muon) the intrinsic-angular-momentum operators are represented by the Pauli matrices multiplied by  

  Sy = (ħ/2) [ [0  −i] ; [i  0] ].

In the problem the constant c is h/4π = ħ/2, and the matrix S that multiplies c is exactly the Pauli matrix σy.  Thus

  Ay = (ħ/2) σy = (ħ/2) [ [0  −i] ; [i  0] ].

1. Ay is a Hermitian operator, so its eigenvalues must be real.  Solving

  Ay |φ⟩ = a |φ⟩

gives a = +ħ/2 or −ħ/2.  Therefore any statement that the eigen-values have non–zero imaginary parts is wrong.

2. Because S = σy anticommutes with σz, an eigenvector of Ay cannot at the same time be an eigenvector of Az = (ħ/2)σz.  However, the total spin operator

  A² = S² = (3/4)ħ² I

commutes with every component, so every spinor (and thus every eigenvector of Ay) is automatically an eigenvector of A² with eigenvalue 3ħ²/4.

Hence the only statement that is correct is:

(C) The eigenfunction of the operator Ay can also be an eigenfunction of A², but not of the Z-component, Az.

Answer: C
